10.title: A changing atmosphere shifts apparent light
10.prompt: Explain why a star and planet can have different twinkling behaviour.
solution: Atmospheric refractive index varies with conditions and height. Starlight can bend so a star appears higher than its geometric position near the horizon.
Turbulence changes the light reaching us from a nearly point-like star, producing twinkling. Planets have an appreciable angular disk, so contributions average and they generally twinkle less.
Planets can still twinkle under some conditions; the source’s “do not twinkle” is an introductory contrast, not an absolute rule.
